scope: Theorem 11.1 (Completion of the metric graph) of the manuscript “Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps” (preprints/Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritical-FK-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e7dab39caf778176), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 108. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In every joint subsequential extraction supplied by Theorems 8.9 and 10.21, one may further extract the intrinsic spaces (Vn, δn) and their spatial distance graphs. Almost surely, every resulting limit of the latter is GD = {(z, w, D(z, w)) : z, w ∈ ˆ︁ C}. (11.2) Consequently (µn, Kn(an)) =⇒ (µ+ , GD+ ) through all positive integers. In any convergent joint extraction with additional reference or local observations, its metric component is the same graph (11.2). The Hausdorff metric for the second component is that induced by ρ(z, z′) + ρ(w, w′) + |r − r′|.
